extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers (U.S., 1943); employers and workers affected by wartime labor regulations
extracted.subtask_description: Associated Press-style newspaper coverage of World War II–era topics: labor controls and regulations, military operations, diplomatic developments, and human-interest items intended to inform the general public and stakeholders (employers, employees, policymakers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Job shift prohibitions under McNutt-Byrnes order
rubrics_metrics.description: Forbid workers employed in essential activities to shift to a non-essential employer or from one essential employer to another at a higher salary or wage rate (determined on a pay-per-hour basis) unless they have been out of the employer's pay for 30 days or more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective one minute after Saturday midnight; directly affects persons employed in essential activities (about 27,000,000). The rule was intended to prevent pay-motivated shifts by essential workers and to encourage movement from non-essential to essential work. Violations by employers or employees carry criminal penalties (see Penalties entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions for release to permit higher-pay shifts
rubrics_metrics.description: An exception allows shifts for higher pay if the old employer will release the worker or the War Manpower Commission (WMC) grants the release itself on the ground that the old employment did not make full-time use of the worker at his highest skill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies especially in areas where the WMC has put into effect an "employment stabilization program" (often described as a "job-freeze plan"). The WMC job-placement unit or the U.S. Employment Service may issue releases when employers refuse. Release may be granted where employee can show his present employment does not utilize highest skill or is not full-time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of "essential activities"
rubrics_metrics.description: "Essential activities" are defined as those listed as such by the War Manpower Commission or designated by its 12 regional directors as "locally needed activities."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This designation determines who is covered by the job-shift prohibitions and by which employers hiring restrictions apply; regional directors may designate activities as locally needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hiring permissions for essential employers
rubrics_metrics.description: Employers in essential activities may hire without restriction anyone not employed in an essential activity during the preceding 30 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision was included to allow essential employers to recruit labor where needed, subject to the 30-day lookback restriction for prior essential-activity employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on non-essential employers hiring from essential activities at higher pay
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-essential employers are forbidden to hire employees away from essential activities at higher pay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restriction was intended to prevent manpower waste by stopping non-essential employers from luring essential workers with higher wages; movement from non-essential to essential work remains encouraged and generally unrestricted.

rubrics_metrics.name: WMC employment-stabilization programs ("job-freezing" plans)
rubrics_metrics.description: Employment-stabilization programs can be put into effect locally by the WMC; these programs frequently require employees moving from one essential activity to another to get a release (a "statement of availability") from the old employer or from the WMC's job-placement unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such programs have been hampered by inadequate WMC staff to patrol hiring on a big scale and thus have been implemented in only some areas. Where in effect, they permit exceptions to the general hiring/shifting prohibitions if proper releases/statements are obtained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for issuance of a "statement of availability"
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement of availability (release) is to be issued wherever the worker: 1) is discharged by his last employer; 2) is laid off for an indefinite period or for seven days or more; or 3) can establish that his present employment does not utilize him at his highest skill or that he is not being employed at full time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement authorizes that the worker may be hired elsewhere in an essential activity; it is central to permitting shifts that would otherwise be prohibited under the order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required content of a "statement of availability"
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement must show the worker’s name, the name and address of the employer or WMC officer, date of issuance, and "a% to the effect that the worker may be hired elsewhere in an essential activity."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order directs that only the required information be included; "The inclusion by an employer on such notice of any information other than that required by this regulation shall be deemed to be a violation." (employer additions are prohibited.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on issuance solely because of lower wages
rubrics_metrics.description: The order forbade issuance of a statement of availability "solely on the ground that the individual’s wage or salary rate is substantially less than that prevailing in the locality for the same or substantially similar work."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A wage-comparative claim by itself does not entitle a worker to a release; releases must be grounded in discharge, layoff, or lack of full-time/highest-skill utilization as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on accepting new employment where prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: No individual shall accept new employment with an employer if that employer is prohibited from hiring the individual under the regulation (i.e., if the hiring would violate the wage-shift prohibitions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Workers are bound by the hiring prohibitions as well as employers; acceptance of illegal hires could subject employees to penalties (see Penalties entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties for violations of McNutt-Byrnes controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Violations by employers or employees of the McNutt-Byrnes order are criminal offenses punishable by penalties as great as a $1,000 fine and one year in prison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order was backed by these criminal penalties to enforce the wage-freeze and hiring-shift restrictions; enforcement effectiveness depends on employer/employee compliance and WMC enforcement capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of existing employee rights and seniority
rubrics_metrics.description: "Nothing in this regulation shall be construed to prejudice existing rights of an employee under any agreement with his employer." The order also included provisions adopted to "protect seniority rights."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These clauses preserve collective-bargaining or contractual rights and seniority systems despite the new hiring and shift restrictions, signaling that the order does not override preexisting employment agreements.
